title: Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling
data_curation: No new data is built. For BrowseComp-Plus the dataset is split into 747 training and 83 test questions, with the static BrowseComp-Plus corpus and index as search backend. For deep research, training uses 1K QA pairs from OpenResearcher with its static browser harness; evaluation on GAIA (text-only subset) and xBench-DeepSearch uses an open web search API. Reward is a binary outcome judged by an LLM (a Qwen3-32B judge on BrowseComp-Plus; a DeepSearchQA-style rubric for deep research). Format gating: an empty or invalid citation line gives the whole rollout reward 0, and out-of-range citations are stripped.
curriculum: Single RL stage from the base models (Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B, Gemma4-E4B, thinking mode); no SFT warm-up. The only schedule is an annealing curriculum on the repeated-failure penalty weight w_f, decayed linearly from 1.5 to 1.0, so strong penalties early discourage repeatedly unsuccessful retrieval and weaker ones later allow exploration. Training runs 115 steps on BrowseComp-Plus and 100 steps for deep research, with 16 prompts x 16 rollouts (256 trajectories) per step split into 8 optimizer updates.
method: Self-Credit builds dense turn-level credit from one sparse outcome reward on top of compaction-augmented GRPO (SUPO-style objective). (1) Self-compaction with citations: when context reaches 16,384 tokens (up to 10 rounds) the policy writes a summary that replaces history and ends with a line citing the few decisive assistant turns (usually 2-5); an auxiliary cited summary is forced for the final segment. (2) Intra-group rescaling: cited turns are matched across the group by retrieved evidence (search turns by docid Jaccard >=0.6, open turns by the same docid), assuming independent turn contributions. Positive-advantage cited turns get w_s=2.5 if cited by >=tau+=2 successes and no failures, 1 if also cited by any failure, else the base beta=1.5; negative-advantage turns get w_f>=1 if cited by >=tau-=2 failures and no successes, else 1. Uncited turns keep w=1; summaries and final answers in successful rollouts are treated as cited. (3) Advantage reweighting: every token in turn t gets A_j * w_t. Optimization: LR 1e-6 constant, clip 0.2/0.28, token-mean loss, no KL, entropy bonus or critic; async rollouts with VeRL + Megatron on 8x8 B200, max 100 turns, 32,768-token responses.
eval_metrics: Pass@1 LLM-judge accuracy over 3 seeds (temperature 0.7) on BrowseComp-Plus (Qwen3-8B/32B, with Qwen3-Embedding-8B retriever), GAIA and xBench-DeepSearch (Gemma4-E4B), against zero-shot, GRPO, GiGPO, SUPO and ECHO, plus average turns. BrowseComp-Plus 32B: Self-Credit 47.0 vs ECHO 41.4, GiGPO 38.2, GRPO 33.3; 8B: 40.6 vs 32.1 (SUPO/ECHO). GAIA 39.2 vs 34.3 (GRPO); xBench-DeepSearch 16.7 vs 12.0 (GiGPO). Analysis metrics: gold documents searched or opened, answer and evidence recall, citation F1 against gold-finding turns and a Claude Sonnet 4.6 judge, and rescaling firing rate and precision. Ablations (32B/8B): no rescaling 41.0/28.9, no repeated-failure penalty 34.9/26.5, credit on all turns 42.2/27.7. OOD average on HotpotQA, MuSiQue, FRAMES and Bamboogle: 46.6 vs 45.4 for GRPO.
key_results: On BrowseComp-Plus, Self-Credit improves Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B by 37.0 and 36.2 points over zero-shot (to 40.6 and 47.0) and beats the strongest RL baselines by 8.5 and 5.6 points. With Gemma4-E4B it beats the best baselines by 4.9 points on GAIA (39.2) and 4.7 points on xBench-DeepSearch (16.7).
evolution_note: Self-Credit combines compaction-augmented agentic RL (SUPO, CompactionRL, ECHO) with group-based turn-level credit in the spirit of GiGPO, but matches turns by the evidence they retrieve rather than by repeated states. It reacts to credit methods that need critics, process reward models, external judges or hindsight rollouts, and to ECHO's success-only turn selection, by using both successful and failed rollouts to correct self-generated credit and guard against citation hacking. It shows that a policy's own summaries can supply usable process supervision for long-horizon search agents.
